To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the diversity in geographic origin of the cord blood collection and banking does not lower the proportion and the quality of validated cord blood unit in our bank.
the diversity of the Mediterranean origins does not have an impact in the quality of the CBU.

1) CB banking from a population highly diverse in geographic origins does not lower CBU qualification rate; 2) CBU qualification rate and CB unit volume and TNC count are independent of ethnic origin; and 3) Mediterranean origins are highly represented among CB and UD registristries.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of the geographic origin of donors on the CBU quality in the Marseille CB bank.
the issue of equality of access of CB units for transplantation in the Marseille region.
the impact of geographic origin and ethnicity on CB qualification rate in a Mediterranean CB bank.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CB banking is an effective way to increase the Haplotype Diversity in the CB Bank and to improve access to HCT for patients from ethnic minorities.
the geographic origin of the donors does not have a significant impact on the qualification rate of CBU in the Marseille Cord Blood Bank.
the geographic origin of CBU donors does not have a significant impact on the qualification rate of CBU.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the geographic origin of CBU donors has no impact on their qualification for transplantation.
the geographic origin of the population has no impact on the qualification rate of CBU.

diversity in the Mediterranean region is not a limiting factor for CB collection, and that CB banking in the Mediterranean region can increase the diversity of the CB Bank and the UD registry, and thus the chances for patients to find a matched donor.

, in a CB Bank with high geographic diversity, CBU qualification is not impaired by geographic origin and does not decrease the number of CBU available for patients.
CB banking from a population of highly diverse geographic origins increases the HLA diversity in CB Bank inventories.
